reason: The reserve needs to be selected at the service panel to protect essential loads during the storm.
expectation: The panel’s essential power slot will be filled, putting the station on reserve.

effect: The station is on reserve, and the next goal is to make the exterior circuits safe.
reaction: The separate shutdown and cooling sequences make the power change feel practical.
reason: The insulated water line corresponds to the panel’s well isolation and drain control, which should protect the exterior water circuit.
expectation: The panel will isolate and drain the well line.

effect: The well is isolated and its exterior line drained before trace heating stops; the fuel fab still needs shutting down.
reaction: The drain-before-heater sequence is a sensible detail.
reason: The running fuel fab matches the panel's shutdown control and is the remaining exterior industrial circuit to secure.
expectation: The panel will shut down the fuel fab safely.

effect: The fuel fab is safely isolated after cooldown, with boil-off vented separately; the exterior-safety goal and chapter are complete.
reaction: The controlled shutdown and unavoidable propellant loss make the storm response feel physically grounded.

mostWorthwhile.text: Draining the well line before switching off its trace heating was the most worthwhile action: it connected a simple panel choice to a clear physical risk and a sensible sequence.

leastWorthwhile.text: Selecting reserve power was straightforward rather than especially engaging, though it established which systems would remain protected.

surprise.text: The fuel tanks retain only part of their liquid while separate vents release boil-off; shutting the plant down does not preserve everything.

arbitrary.text: None of the three actions felt arbitrary: each corresponded to a named panel control and a storm-preparation goal.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how the station and its samples fare after the storm; the shutdown details gave that outcome practical stakes.
